events.summary: Speaker D reported from the user survey that users find remote controls very ugly.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: First of all, they find it very ugly

events.summary: Speaker D reported that people seem ready to pay more for a nice, fancy looking remote.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: people are ready to pay for nice and look and fancy looking

events.summary: Speaker D proposed making zapping through channels easy, because users zap very often.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: it should be easy for them to to zap

events.summary: Speaker D proposed making the most used buttons easier to see and use than the rarely used ones.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: some of the buttons which are those that are used should be easier to see and use than others

events.summary: Speaker D proposed a way to ask the remote where it is, like finding a phone.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: something where we could ask the remote control please, where are you

events.summary: Speaker D reported that most people do not know how to use the many buttons on their remote.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: most of the the people say they they don't know how to they to use properly

events.summary: Speaker B cited that 26 percent of people complain the remote is bad for repetitive strain injury.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: But twenty six percent, do you know

events.summary: Speaker D reported that people find teletext relevant, though it is used less than channel selection.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: It seems that people find teletext teletext uh relevant, even if I personally never use it

events.summary: Speaker D said teletext scored six out of ten on relevance in the survey.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: people scored a six on this

events.summary: Speaker D reported that young people find speech recognition very relevant, and relevance goes down with age.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: Young people, probably because it's a buzz word, find it very relevant

events.summary: Speaker D proposed considering speech recognition if the target is young people.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: I think if we are targeting young people then uh it's probably something we have to consider

events.summary: Speaker D said the group should aim at young people, who are the early adopters of new devices.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: I think we should aim at the young people

events.summary: Speaker D said teletext is probably useless for young people, who have other ways to find information.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: Then teletext is useless for them I think, yeah

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a simple design principle, following Occam's razor: make only a remote control and nothing more.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: We should never complicate things too much

events.summary: Speaker B proposed only on and off, volume, channels, and maybe some options as buttons.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Only buttons we need is on off, volume, channels and maybe some options

events.summary: Speaker B said the design must be simple, since the company puts fashion into electronics and simple remotes lead this market.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Be simple. Be simple and you'll lean on this market

events.summary: Speaker B proposed titanium, because it is a good style, unbreakable and universal, for a baby-proof remote.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: to make a baby-proof remote control it got to be a titanium

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a screen with a backlight that can change colours, so the remote is easy to find.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: We'll have a screen with a back light which can change colours

events.summary: Speaker B proposed few buttons that can be found by touch, with the options controlled through the screen.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: And all these buttons should be easy to find and to click

events.summary: Speaker B proposed fully automatic power on and off, so the TV turns on when the user takes the remote to the sofa.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: power on and off can be made fully automatic

events.summary: Speaker B proposed volume that adjusts with the distance to the TV, so it stays right when the user moves around the room.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Suppose you set u you set up some volume and then you move out

events.summary: Speaker B proposed making the remote universal, for example for a hi-fi system.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Let it be universal, so you want to use it for your hi-fi system

events.summary: Speaker A decided to concentrate only on the TV remote for now, and make it more general later.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we will only concentrate on T_V_ for the moment

events.summary: Speaker B proposed setting the TV to the four or five channels the user actually uses, so channel 25 is never needed.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Basically you use just four or five channels, right

events.summary: Speaker D proposed a next button that cycles through a chosen set of favourite channels.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: you could just say these are the cha ch channel three, twenty eight, forty eight

events.summary: Speaker D objected that people like to zap through all the channels, so limiting to four or five does not fit how they use the remote.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: they want to zap out of the one hundred channels

events.summary: Speaker A proposed different modes for each button, such as a zapping mode.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: Maybe we can make uh different modes for each button and you can change mode zapping mode or

events.summary: Speaker C said that if the remote is universal, the functions for each device must be limited.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: then we ought to limit for functions for each of our devices

events.summary: Speaker D will check with the department whether there is research on how many people go to channels such as 25 and 64.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: Well I could could uh have a look at that maybe

events.summary: Speaker C reported the working design needs few components: the battery, the user interface, a digital signal processing chip and the infrared LED.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: so we need few components, mainly the energy source like the battery

events.summary: Speaker C proposed a simple speech recogniser on the signal processing chip, trained for the user.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: simple speech recogniser on our D_S_B_ chip

events.summary: Speaker C estimated the component cost at five Euros or less, because the device is simple and made in bulk.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we can make it in five Euros and even less than that

events.summary: Speaker B said the budget is about twelve Euros for this.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: for this budget like twelve Euros

events.summary: Speaker B proposed gesture recognition, such as rolling the remote to change volume.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Did you consider the r gest uh gesture recognition

events.summary: Speaker C objected that gesture recognition is very expensive for a target of about twelve point five Euros.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: this point we didn't consider because it's it's very expensive

events.summary: Speaker C said the target is about twelve point five Euros.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: our target is only like twelve point five Euros

events.summary: Speaker C objected that automatic on and off is a bit problematic, because people have different criteria for when to switch off.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: even automatic on off is also a bit problematic

events.summary: Speaker D proposed a personalised remote for each user, with their own settings, since a room may have more than one remote.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: should we target a a user personalised uh uh remote control

events.summary: Speaker A objected that personal settings may cause arguments in the household.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: Wouldn't that make uh arguments? I want uh

events.summary: Speaker A said automatic on and off is not possible for now, and Speaker C agreed it is not in the current price.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: I think automatic on off control uh it's not possible

events.summary: Speaker B proposed speakers in the remote, so the user can shout to find it.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: should it be equipped with the uh, with uh speakers

events.summary: Speaker D proposed a simple beep as enough to find the remote, since it is very cheap.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: It just beeps. That would be enough

events.summary: Speaker C objected that a remote that always listens would use a lot of power, because it must always be on.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: it really consumes because it should be all the time on

events.summary: Speaker D proposed finding the remote by whistling or clapping, since devices already respond to those sounds.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: I heard of devices where you just uh whistle them

events.summary: Speaker D objected that a one-hand clap or whistle feature does not suit the target people.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: These are not our target people

events.summary: Speaker B objected that clap activation may interfere with other devices, such as lights that turn on with clapping.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: like all these people do that their lights are turning on with clapping
